**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against The Associated Press:

- Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned zero hits.
- A full read of the document's single operative section (§§ 1–14, p0000–p0074) confirms no clause lets Kubient examine our books, usage, or systems.
- The only access-flavoured language is § 1's ordinary cooperation covenant ("Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services"), which is service-delivery cooperation, not an audit right. § 6 (Use of Service) imposes use restrictions but no self-certification or inspection mechanic, and § 12 (Confidentiality) contains no audit hook.

Because AUDIT is a defensive rule, absence of any audit right is better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so no edit is warranted.

One flag for a different rule (opposite direction, so not redlined here): § 3(e) defines Impressions as measured **by Kubient**, and § 5 revenue share depends on Kubient's collections, yet AP has no right to verify Kubient's measurement or payment records. If your playbook has a vendor-side records/audit rule, that gap is worth pursuing there.
